claim(uint256,address,uint256,bytes32[]).details: Anyone may submit the proof, but the tokens only ever go to the account in the leaf. That lets us pay the gas for a contributor who has none without being able to redirect what they are owed.

openRound(bytes32,uint256,uint64).details: Funding is checked rather than pulled: the launch transaction transfers the contributor pool in and opens the round in the same call, and a distributor that could pull would need an allowance from something that has one.

sweep(uint256).details: `block.timestamp` is compared here and in `claim`, which the linter flags. It is the right clock for both: a validator can move it by seconds, and these windows are a six-month lock and a one-year sweep delay. Block numbers would be worse — they drift against wall time, and a lock a contributor was told lasts six months should last six months.Deliberately late and deliberately to one address, the network's treasury. Unclaimed value that can never be recovered is a slow leak; unclaimed value that can be recovered early is a reason not to trust the distributor at all.Never before the round unlocks, whichever of the two clocks runs later. The delay counts from the round opening and is one number the deployer sets for every launch; the lock is another, set per launch by policy; nothing checks one against the other, and a lock longer than the delay would otherwise let the treasury empty a round no contributor could yet touch. Waited out here rather than refused in `openRound`: a long lock is a legitimate choice and not a mistake, and refusing it would revert the whole launch over a constant somebody has to go and change, when the only correct answer to it is to wait.

fees().notice: The chain's fee settings, which name the treasury.

openRound(bytes32,uint256,uint64).notice: Opens a round against tokens this contract already holds.

opener().notice: The factory that made it: it may open the first round, and nothing after.

reserved().notice: Tokens still owed by all open rounds. A new round must have its own funding.

sweep(uint256).notice: Sends what a round's claimants never took to the treasury. Anyone may call it once the round's delay is up: the tokens can go only to the treasury `LaunchFees` names at that moment.

sweepDelay().notice: How long after a round opens before what is left may be swept. Never before the round unlocks, whatever this says: see `sweep`.

treasury().notice: Where unclaimed value goes, and who may open a later round: the chain's treasury now.
